name: ac-coverage-decomposed
why:
The treatment arm for the co-adaptation question. `ac-coverage` asks one call to hold `ac-audit-rubric` — six checks, five verdicts, a precedence table — and emit three verdicts. Premium models score 100%; the open-weight roster scores 30%. That gap is capability PLUS co-adaptation: the prompts were authored and iterated against frontier models for months, and assume a reader who can apply a dense rubric in one pass.

This arm asks the identical evidence in the identical words, restructured: three binary questions per criterion, each with its own minimal prompt and a one-token contract, and **the verdict computed in code from the answers**. No rubric is shown; no verdict vocabulary is required of the model.

That is `capability-tiered-duties-plan.md`'s thesis made testable. If decomposition closes most of the gap, the framework becomes portable by being restructured rather than by buying better models, and workstreams A/F stop being cost optimisations and become the migration itself. If it closes little, that is a real capability floor and the search budget belongs on finding stronger open weights.

criteria.AC-1: `getById` returns null for a missing order.
criteria.AC-2: `getById` logs a warning when the order is missing.
criteria.AC-3: `getById` retries once on a network timeout.
